newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo says pledged 30 bln rand to S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Anglo says pledged 30 bln rand to S.Africa.

text.p: As a sign of its belief in South Africa, Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd has committed some 30 billion rand in its home country over the next five years, deputy chairman Nicky Oppenheimer said.

"...Anglo Amercan and its associates have capital commitments in South Africa to the year 2001 of some 30 billion rand -- firm evidence, surely, of our commitment to and confidence in the new South Africa and its institutions," Oppenheimer said on Tuesday.
Addressing a South Africa investment conference in London, he said the country's export potential was the key factor in determining the attractiveness of new industrial investments.

Anglo's policy was to concentrate on products which could compete internationally, many of which also benefitted from South Africa's low-cost power. These included automotive components, chemical products, food and bevergaes, paper and pulp and fabricated medtal products.

Oppenheimer said European investors had been somewhat slow in perceiving the real opportunities which existed in South Africa, especially now that it had escaped the constraints of a small and stratified domestic market.
"Certainly, the rest of Africa remains a relatively small item on South Africa's export table, but trade with the rest of the continent is growing at a rate that should tempt any investor," he said.
Oppenheimer said South African exports to Africa last year increased by 60 percent.
He urged investors not to wait too long before exploring opportunities in South Africa which he said now offered a far better investment climate than in the apartheid years.
"It may still be far from perfect, but investors who wait until all the risks have been overcome will find that their rewards, too, have been commensurately diminished."
